content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: A step can expose values through `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`; a job can publish named outputs to downstream jobs through the `needs` context. `run` executes shell commands while `uses` invokes an action. Keep steps small, name them clearly, validate inputs, and review third-party action code and permissions. The most useful check is one that produces observable evidence and fails clearly when its stated requirement is not met.

items.title: Step output identifiers
items.text: Write one step output as `name=value` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, then declare job outputs if a downstream job needs the value. Use `$GITHUB_ENV` for values needed by later steps in the same job.

items.title: Sharing computed values between workflow stages
items.text: Use filters to reduce unnecessary runs only when skipped work is genuinely unrelated. Include shared dependencies and test the changed and unchanged path cases so required checks are not bypassed.

content_blocks.code:
name: Pass a value between jobs
on: workflow_dispatch
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      build_label: ${{ steps.label.outputs.build_label }}
    steps:
      - id: label
        run: echo "build_label=demo-${GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  report:
    needs: prepare
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          LABEL: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.build_label }}
        run: echo "Prepared $LABEL"
content_blocks.expected_output: The first job writes a named step output, exposes it as a job output, and the dependent job reads it through `needs`.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Dispatch the workflow and inspect both jobs. Confirm the output name matches at each step.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Avoid using outputs for secrets or large files; use an approved secret mechanism or artifact for those cases.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain understanding action outputs, read the example, and identify a way to validate it. The wider system goal remains: Decide when to run a shell command, invoke an action, or move logic into a repository script.

content.expected_output: The expected result is the behavior described here: A step can expose values through `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`; a job can publish named outputs to downstream jobs through the `needs` context. The real result depends on the repository, selected ref, configured permissions, and runner availability.
troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
